We assume the fleet shrinks to zero by December 31, as the CFO guided, but the hashprice rose 6.9% from the June quarter.\n- Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $69.0M (28.8% margin), up from $19.2M, even after the guided $40M to $50M jump in cash SG&A.\n- We forecast Q2 FY27 revenue of $403.9M, 3.0% above the $392.0M consensus, but the CFO warned that most December capacity comes \"late in the quarter\". If it all slips to the last two weeks, Q2 falls to $381.0M.\n- Funding is the overhang: $25B to $30B of FY27 capex against about $14B secured, and 394.1M shares outstanding in August, up 39.0% from about 283.5M a year earlier.\n- Short interest was 81.7M shares (20.7% of shares outstanding) on September 30, and the stock has moved an average of 9.4% the day after its last five reports.\n\nIREN: Quarterly revenue, Q1 FY25 to Q2 FY27F\n\n On this page \n\nIREN (IREN $25.43 +2.11%) reports Q1 FY27 results on November 5, 2026. IREN's fiscal year ends June 30, so the report covers July to September 2026, the first quarter in which Microsoft's Horizon 1 cluster earned revenue. The stock goes into the print at $24.91, down 39.1% since September 30 and 67.4% below its closing high of $76.41 a year earlier, after a sell-off that hit every company borrowing to build GPU clouds.\n\nWe rebuilt the quarter from the run-rate figures management gave on the August 27 call. Our answer: Q1 revenue should beat consensus, because the company said its operating ARR doubled to $1 billion in mid-August and would stay there through September, while the Bitcoin mining business it is winding down still earned money at a better hashprice. The December quarter looks closer to consensus, since most new capacity arrives late in the quarter. The real debate is no longer revenue. It is how IREN pays for a $25 to $30 billion capital plan without selling much more stock at today's price.\n\n## The data behind this piece \n\n Explore the primary data Equibles carries for IREN: \n\n## Why Q1 should beat consensus\n\nIREN's revenue fell for three straight quarters as it switched off Bitcoin miners to make room for GPUs. The June quarter was the low point at $137.2M. The September quarter is where the AI Cloud ramp should overtake the mining decline, and management gave unusually precise inputs to model it.\n\nOn the August 27 call, CFO Anthony Lewis said IREN \"exited Q4 at roughly half a billion of ARR\", that ARR was \"$1 billion today following acceptance of Horizon 1 by Microsoft\", and that it \"will carry through to the end of the September quarter\". The Microsoft contract is worth $9.7 billion over five years, about $1.94 billion a year across four identical 50 MW deployments, so each Horizon carries about $485M of ARR. IREN announced on August 13 that Microsoft had accepted Horizon 1.\n\nThat gives a simple calculation:\n\n- Existing capacity: $0.5 billion of ARR for all 92 days of the quarter is $126.0M.\n- Horizon 1: $485M of ARR for the 49 days from August 13 to September 30 is $65.1M.\n- AI Cloud total:$191.1M, up from $70.5M in the June quarter.\n\nConsensus of $221.3M leaves about $172M for AI Cloud if mining comes in near our estimate, which implies either a later start for Horizon 1 or existing GPUs earning well below their run-rate. Neither is what management described.\n\nIREN: Operating AI Cloud ARR\n\n### Bitcoin mining: shrinking, but at a better price\n\nIREN no longer publishes monthly mining updates, so we estimated the fleet from public Bitcoin network data. Dividing each quarter's mining revenue by the network's revenue per unit of hashrate gives the effective hashrate IREN earned on:\n\n- Q3 FY26 (January to March): $111.2M at an average hashprice of $36.1 per PH/s per day, about 34.3 EH/s.\n- Q4 FY26 (April to June): $66.7M at $35.7, about 20.6 EH/s.\n- Q1 FY27 (July to September): the hashprice averaged $38.1, up 6.9%, because the network's hashrate fell from 956 to 918 EH/s while the Bitcoin price held near $71,000.\n\nThe 10-K puts installed mining capacity at 23.2 EH/s on June 30, and the CFO expects mining \"to be effectively decommissioned by the end of December 2026\". We assume about 80% of the installed fleet was earning on July 1 (18.6 EH/s) and that it falls in a straight line to zero by December 31. That averages 13.9 EH/s in the September quarter and $48.8M of revenue. Each 1 EH/s of average hashrate is worth about $3.5M of quarterly revenue at Q1's hashprice.\n\nI","highlights":["Equibles Research · Research thesis· October 26, 2026· 13 min read\n\n## Summary\n\n- We forecast Q1 FY27 revenue of $239.9M, 8.4% above the $221.3M consensus (13 analysts, as of October 17) and near the top of the $200.0M to $244.6M range.\n- AI Cloud revenue of $191.1M: $126.0M from the roughly $0.5 billion of ARR IREN exited June with, plus $65.1M from Horizon 1, whose $485M share of the Microsoft contract started on August 13.\n- Bitcoin mining revenue of $48.8M, down from $66.7M. Neither is what management described.\n\n...\n\nIREN had $7.6 billion of cash on June 30, including $1.7 billion of restricted cash. In the June quarter alone it raised $3.0 billion of convertible notes and $2.1 billion from share sales, and customer prepayments pushed operating cash flow to $1.8 billion. Deferred revenue stood at $1.84 billion and remaining performance obligations at $5.1 billion.\n\nThe problem is the size of the plan. The CFO put FY27 capital expenditure at $25 to $30 billion, covering the 2026 deployments behind the $4 billion ARR target, the air-cooled 2027 capacity and much of the liquid-cooled 2027 data centers. Against that, he counted about $14 billion as secured (cash, committed financing and prepayments) plus an estimated $8 billion of additional GPU-related financing. That still leaves $3 billion to $8 billion to find.\n\nThe cost of debt is rising too. The balance of points shown with the takes weighs what the document actually discloses, so the two can disagree, for example when a trial that missed its main goal is described in upbeat language.\n\nHow Sentiment works How the balance works\n\n## Rhea-AI Filing Summary\n\nIREN Ltd (IREN) reported full-year results for the year ended June 30, 2026, highlighting a major pivot from Bitcoin mining to AI Cloud Services. Total revenue was $707.0m, up from $501.0m in FY25, driven by AI Cloud Services revenue of $128.8m, which increased roughly eight-fold from $16.4m, while Bitcoin mining revenue rose to $578.2m from $484.6m.\n\nThe company posted a net loss of $702.6m versus net income of $86.9m a year earlier, largely due to $638.8m of non-cash asset impairments tied mainly to decommissioned Bitcoin mining hardware as sites are repurposed for AI. Adjusted EBITDA was $245.7m, down from $269.7m, with margins compressed by higher staffing and platform investments.\n\nManagement emphasized rapid growth in its AI infrastructure platform, citing $4bn contracted annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) for 2026 capacity and $1bn operating ARR. IREN reported $14bn of existing cash, committed GPU financing and prepayments, including major GPU financings of $3.6bn and $2.8bn, and year-end cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $7,619.5m, alongside substantial capex and higher debt supporting global data center expansion.\n\n### Positive\n\n- Total revenue grew to $707.0m from $501.0m, reflecting strong topline expansion during the pivot toward AI Cloud Services.\n- AI Cloud Services revenue rose to $128.8m from $16.4m, an ~8x increase as the new business line gains traction.\n- Contracted ARR reached $4bn for 2026 capacity with $1bn operating ARR, indicating significant visibility into future AI-related revenues.\n- Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash reached $7,619.5m at year-end, supported by sizeable equity and debt raises and GPU financings.\n- Secured $3.6bn and $2.8bn of GPU financings, largely funding associated GPU capex and supporting data center growth.\n\n### Negative\n\n- Net loss was $702.6m versus net income of $86.9m in the prior year, a sharp deterioration in bottom-line results.\n- Non-cash impairments totaled $638.8m, primarily from decommissioning Bitcoin mining hardware as sites are converted to AI use.\n- Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $245.7m from $269.7m, with margin falling to 35% from 54% amid higher operating and investment costs.\n- Operating cash outflows for investing activities were $4,723.0m, reflecting very heavy capex for property, hardware, and intangibles.\n- Total debt rose to $7,593.0m (current and non-current), significantly increasing the company’s leverage profile.\n\n## Filing Explained\n\nOnly $1 billion of the stated $4 billion 2026 ARR is operating today; the remainder depends on commissioning, testing, and customer acceptance.\n\nThis Form 8-K reports IREN’s fourth-quarter and fiscal-year results and related business update. The company highlights \n\n$4bn\n\n of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity versus \n\n$1bn\n\n of operating ARR today; ARR is an operating metric, not GAAP revenue.\n\nThe \n\n$4bn\n\n figure is targeted to be operational by \n\nDecember 31, 2026\n\n, subject to commissioning, testing and customer acceptance, so the disclosed contracted capacity has not all reached the operating stage.\n\nThe financing disclosed includes \n\n$3.6bn\n\n for the Microsoft contract, funding \n\n96%\n\n of associated GPU capex with prepayments, and \n\n$2.8bn\n\n for other deployments; the latter includes \n\n$2.4bn\n\n at a \n\n9.0%\n\n fixed rate and funds \n\n90%\n\n of associated GPU capex.\n\nCustomer prepayments are amounts payable in advance of service delivery, and the filing says they represent \n\n45–55%\n\n of estimated GPU and ancillary capex; terms vary by contract and future contracts may not include them.\n\nThe cash-flow statement records \n\n$4,742.8m\n\n of proceeds from issuing Ordinary shares, which increases the share count and reduces an existing holder’s percentage ownership absent offsetting changes.\n\nOperationally, Horizon 1 has been delivered to Microsoft, Horizon 2 commissioning is underway, and Horizons 3–4 are in late-stage construction targeted for delivery in Q4 2026.\n\nThe named milestones to monitor are Horizon 2 commissioning and the Q4 2026 Transcribing","text":"IREN (IREN) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript | The Motley Fool\n\nImage source: The Motley Fool.\n\n## DATE\n\nThursday, Aug. 27, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET\n\n## CALL PARTICIPANTS\n\n- Vice President, Investor Relations - Mike Power\n- Co-Founder and Co-Chief Executive Officer - Daniel Roberts\n- Chief Financial Officer - Anthony Lewis\n- Chief Commercial Officer - Kent Draper\n\n## TAKEAWAYS\n\n- Annualized Run-Rate Revenue (ARR) -- $4 billion in contracted revenue for 2026 capacity and $1 billion in current operating revenue, reflecting the delivery of Horizon 1 to Microsoft.\n- Total Revenue -- $137.2 million for the fourth quarter, representing a decrease of $7.6 million from the prior quarter as the company decommissioned mining hardware to install GPUs.\n- AI Cloud Services Revenue -- $70.5 million for the quarter, up from $33.6 million in the prior quarter, driven by the ramp of new customer deployments.\n- Net Loss -- $684 million for the fourth quarter, primarily due to non-cash impairments of $450.4 million related to decommissioned Bitcoin mining hardware.\n- Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA -- $19.2 million for the quarter, down from $59.5 million in the prior quarter because of increased employee costs and platform investment.\n- Contracted Pricing -- 3-year contracts are pricing above $20 million per megawatt of IT load, which represents an approximate 2-year payback period on compute investments.\n- Pricing Outlook -- Management reported active discussions for new contracts at approximately $25 million per megawatt of IT load, indicating continued upward pressure on pricing.\n- GPU Financing -- $6.5 billion in total financing secured over the last three months, including $3.6 billion of investment-grade funding at a 6% interest rate.\n- Non-Investment Grade Financing -- $2.8 billion in equipment financing closed at a 9% fixed rate, including a $2.4 billion facility led by Blue Owl and PIMCO for the Mackenzie expansion.\n- Customer Prepayments -- 45% to 55% of GPU capital expenditures on recent deals are funded via prepayments, which contributes to a surplus of funding for data center costs.\n- Fiscal Year 2027 CapEx Guidance -- $25 billion to $30 billion estimated, covering Microsoft capacity delivery and data center construction for 2027 and 2028 projects.\n- Total Funding Capacity -- $14 billion in total cash and committed GPU financing available as of the results date, including $7.6 billion of cash on the balance sheet at June 30.\n- Capacity Targets -- Management is targeting 300 megawatts of IT load in 2026 and 800 megawatts in 2027, reaching 1.2 gigawatts of gross capacity.\n- Data Center Pipeline -- 5 gigawatts of secured grid connections currently announced, representing more than 10 times the company's currently contracted capacity.\n- Headcount Growth -- The workforce nearly tripled in fiscal year 2026, and management expects similar growth in fiscal year 2027 to support scaling operations.\n- Operating Expenses -- Cash SG&A is expected to increase by $40 million to $50 million sequentially in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 due to investments in R&D and marketing.\n- Bitcoin Mining Decommissioning -- Management expects mining operations to be effectively discontinued by the end of December 2026 as facilities transition to AI cloud services.\n- Hardware Deployment -- Horizon 1, the first of four 50-megawatt liquid-cooled deployments, was delivered to Microsoft in August 2026.\n- Unencumbered Assets -- 100% of the company's data center portfolio remains unencumbered, providing a future opportunity for asset-backed financing as projects stabilize.\n- Site Optimization -- The company plans to convert all Canal Flats capacity to liquid-cooling for GB300 GPUs to maximize value from existing power assets.\n\n## RISKS\n\n- CFO Anthony Lewis stated that the actual capital expenditures for the year would depend on a range of factors, including \"final costings, construction schedules, delivery time lines for GPUs and long lead items.\"\n- Management reported $638.8 million in non-cash impairments for the full fiscal year, which Lewis attributed to \"the decommissioning of Bitcoin mining hardware as sites are converted to support AI Cloud growth.\"\n- Roberts noted that while the company owns its infrastructure, the build-out of physical assets such as power, land, and data centers \"take years to permit, finance and build,\" which creates lead-time constraints against surging digital demand.\n\n## SUMMARY\n\nManagement reported a strategic transition from Bitcoin mining to a vertically integrated AI cloud platform, noting that its 2026 capacity is now largely sold out. The company stated that it owns the entire stack including land, power, data centers, compute, and software, which management believes increases the value of its grid connections. IREN confirmed the delivery of its first major liquid-cooled deployment to Microsoft and secured significant GPU financing across both investment-grade and non-investment-grade tiers. projects stabilize.\n- Site Optimization -- The company plans to convert all Canal Flats capacity to liquid-cooling for GB300 GPUs to maximize value from existing power assets.\n\n...\n\nAnthony Lewis: Thanks, Dan, and good evening, everyone. Over the past 12 months, we have secured circa $19 billion in funding, nearly $16 billion across customer prepayments, GPU financing and convertible notes alongside equity of approximately $3 billion. The vast majority of this funding is either in cash or yet to be drawn down, giving us significant capacity. For FY '27, we're guiding CapEx of approximately $25 billion to $30 billion. Included in that estimate is delivery of the contracted Microsoft capacity, the other deployments to deliver on 2026 ARR and GPU and data center CapEx for air-cooled deployments scheduled across calendar year 2027.\n\nIt will also support new liquid-cooled data center capacity at Childress and Sweetwater 1 for delivery in the second half of calendar year 2027 as well as earlier stage investment for 2028 and beyond. Of course, the actual CapEx for the year will depend on a range of factors, including final costings, construction schedules, delivery time lines for GPUs and long lead items, the overall contracting environment and the overall fundraising environment. Within that CapEx estimate, we expect data center and CapEx GPU requirements to be up approximately 15% to 20% for ongoing and new deployments with revenue increases expected to ultimately outpace those increases. In respect to the funding plan, as noted earlier, we have a strong starting position.\n\nApproximately $14 billion of existing cash and committed GPU financing and prepayments. That includes $7.6 billion of cash on the balance sheet at 30 June, of which $1.7 billion is restricted with most of that $1.7 billion set aside to fund Microsoft GPU CapEx. We're targeting roughly an additional $8 billion of GPU financing and prepayments in support of GPU CapEx requirements, noting the healthy prepayments that we are seeing in recent contracting and the growing market for GPU financing that Dan has spoken to. The balance of the requirement we expect to meet through data center financing, operating cash flows and corporate sources.\n\n...\n\nOn data center financing, as Dan has spoken to, our entire data center portfolio is unencumbered today, including Horizons 1 through 4. So there is obviously a significant and growing asset base to raise asset finance against. Alongside the growing market for GPU financing, attractive customer prepayments, we feel well placed to scale our fundraising efforts to support the rapid growth of the platform. Now turning to the quarter 4 results and outlook. The quarter's results continue to reflect the ongoing transition to AI cloud. For the June quarter, revenue was $137.2 million, including AI cloud revenue of $70.5 million.\n\nThis was down $7.6 million compared to the prior quarter as we decommissioned mining hardware ahead of GPU installations, partially offset by AI cloud growth. Cost of revenue also fell $6.6 million, mainly as a result of lower electricity usage from reduced mining activities. Net loss was $684 million for the quarter, largely driven by noncash impairments of $450.4 million, mostly on account of decommissioning mining hardware, plus a $102.1 million decrease in fair value of mining hardware held for sale, both reflecting costs of transitioning our existing sites to AI cloud. We currently expect mining operations to be effectively decommissioned by the end of December 2026.\n\nWe expect first quarter cash SG&A to increase approximately $40 million to $50 million sequentially as we continue to invest for growth across sales and marketing, R&D, development, site and cloud operations and other functions ahead of significant revenue growth over the coming periods, which brings me to ARR. We exited Q4 at roughly $0.5 billion of ARR. It's $1 billion today following acceptance of Horizon 1 by Microsoft, and that will carry through to the end of the September quarter. And we expect more than $4 billion of ARR by the end of the December quarter, which is already under contract and includes delivery of Horizons 2 through 4.\n\nA significant amount of the December capacity is expected to come on late in the quarter, so we will see the reported revenue effect come through predominantly in the March quarter. The company also reported a net loss of $684 million, driven largely by non-cash impairments tied to the planned exit from bitcoin mining. Shares, which had closed the regular session at $40.53, fell 7.23% in after-hours trading to $37.6, suggesting investors focused on the revenue miss and heavy loss despite the company’s stronger long-term growth outlook.\n\n## Key Takeaways\n\n- AI Cloud revenue reached $70.5 million, or 51.4% of total revenue, showing the company’s shift away from mining.\n- IREN ended the quarter with about $500 million in annual recurring revenue, which rose to $1 billion after Microsoft accepted Horizon 1.\n- The company said more than $4 billion of ARR is expected by the December quarter and is already under contract.\n- Management said it secured about $19 billion in funding over the past 12 months through customer prepayments, GPU financing, convertible notes and equity.\n- Shares fell in after-hours trading even after a 2.4% gain during the regular session.\n\n## Company Performance\n\nIREN’s results showed a company in the middle of a major transformation. Revenue declined sequentially by $7.6 million as management deliberately decommissioned mining hardware ahead of new GPU installations. At the same time, AI Cloud revenue kept rising and became the largest part of the business.\n\nThe company’s strategy is to move from bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure, where it owns data centers, power, compute and software. Management said this full-stack model gives it an advantage because each layer adds value to the one below it. The company also said it now has $4 billion of ARR contracted for 2026 capacity, with $1 billion already operating today.\n\nThe quarter included a large accounting loss tied to the mining exit. IREN said the net loss reflected $450.4 million in impairments related to decommissioned mining hardware and a $102.1 million decline in the fair value of mining hardware held for sale.\n\n## Financial Highlights\n\n- Revenue: $137.2 million in Q4 FY2026, down $7.6 million sequentially.\n- AI Cloud revenue: $70.5 million, or 51.4% of total revenue.\n- Net loss: $684 million, mainly due to non-cash impairment charges.\n- Mining hardware impairment: $450.4 million.\n- Fair value decline on mining hardware held for sale: $102.1 million.\n- Cost of revenue: down $6.6 million in the quarter, helped by lower electricity use.\n- ARR at quarter end: about $500 million.\n- ARR after Microsoft Horizon 1 acceptance: $1 billion.\n- Funding secured over 12 months: about $19 billion.\n- Cash on balance sheet at June 30, 2026: $7.6 billion, including $1.7 billion restricted.\n\n## Earnings vs. Forecast\n\nIREN did not provide an EPS figure in the information available, but revenue can be compared with the market forecast. Analysts expected $157.14 million in revenue, while the company reported $137.2 million. That is a shortfall of $19.94 million, or about 12.7% below expectations.\n\nThe miss is notable because investors have been watching for evidence that the AI cloud transition is translating into faster top-line growth. Instead, the quarter showed that revenue is still being affected by the planned reduction in mining activity. The company’s large loss also likely added to the disappointment, even though much of it was non-cash and linked to the strategic shift.\n\n## Market Reaction\n\nThe stock’s reaction was mixed but turned negative after the report. IREN closed the regular session at $40.53, up 2.4% from the prior close of $39.58. In after-hours trading, however, the shares fell to $37.6, down 7.23% from the close and about 5% below the previous day’s close.\n\nThe move left the stock well above its 52-week low of $22.63, but still far below its 52-week high of $76.87. That wide range reflects the market’s uncertainty about how quickly IREN can convert its AI infrastructure buildout into sustained profits. No trading volume data was provided, so it is not possible to determine whether the move came with unusually heavy activity.\n\n## Outlook & Guidance\n\nManagement gave a very ambitious outlook for the next year. IREN said it expects more than $4 billion of ARR by the December quarter, up from about $500 million at the end of Q4 and $1 billion after Microsoft accepted Horizon 1. The company also said about $700 million of ARR tied to an NVIDIA cloud contract is expected to ramp in 2027. DCD\n\n# Iren secures contract from \"leading frontier lab,\" on track to exit crypto business by end of year\n\nNeocloud releases results for fiscal year 2026\n\nSeptember 02, 2026\n\nBy\n: Georgia Butler \n\nIren, formerly Iris Energy, has secured a cloud contract with an unnamed \"leading frontier lab,\" as the company released its full-year results for FY2026.\n\nSpeaking during the company's earnings call, co-founder and co-CEO Daniel Roberts noted that the company now has annual recurring revenue (ARR) of $4 billion, including contracts with the likes of Cohere, Prometheus, Perplexity, Figure AI, Fal.ai, and Higgsfield AI.\n\nHe added that, of that ARR, $1 billion is currently operating and is expected to ramp up during 2027, including a further $700 million associated with Iren's contract with Nvidia, which was signed in May 2026, and spans five years with a total contract value of $3.4bn.\n\n \n\nAccording to Iren's Annual Report filing with the SEC, this, along with the company's $9.7bn cloud deal signed with Microsoft in November 2025, \"represent[s] a substantial majority of our contracted revenue.\" The first phase of capacity for that contract was delivered in August 2026.\n\nIt goes on to note: \"The loss of, or any material reduction in committed capacity by, any significant customer, or any failure by a significant customer to accept capacity or perform its payment or other obligations, could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and cash flows.\"\n\nIren's remaining performance obligations are valued at $16.6bn, while the aggregate contracted value of lease arrangements was approximately $11.4 billion.\n\nIren has been publicly listed since 2021, though previously focused on its Bitcoin mining operations. This is the first full year of operations in which the company has placed its AI cloud efforts front and center, and with that in mind, Iren is currently set to be \"effectively decommissioned\" by the end of December 2026.\n\nWhile this is the aim, Iren still derives the vast majority of its revenue from its Bitcoin mining operations.\n\nThe company's Bitcoin mining capacity sits around 380MW at present, while its AI cloud capacity was just 40MW as of the end of June 2026. For the full year, AI cloud revenue was $128.8m, up from $16.4m in 2025, while Bitcoin mining brought in $578.2m, up from $501m the year prior. Iren typically liquidates its Bitcoin on a daily basis, converting the proceeds into fiat currency to fund its operating and capital expenditures.\n\nTogether, this brings the company's full operating capacity to 420MW, while it has a pipeline of 5GW planned across sites in British Columbia, Canada (x3 and 160MW); Texas, US (x3 and 2.75GW); Oklahoma, US (1.6GW); Bundey, Australia (800MW), and Badajoz, Spain (300MW).\n\nIt is noted by Iren that there is some degree of risk associated with changing its strategy: \"Any potential further expansion of AI cloud services or expansion into additional markets will take time to implement, and there can be no assurance that we will be successful in doing so in the near term or at all.\"\n\nWhile revenue for both Bitcoin mining and AI cloud services was up Year-on-Year (YoY), Iren posted a net loss of $702.6 million, while the year prior had a net profit of $86.9m.\n\nThis was largely related to the increasing operating expenses, which reached $1.534bn in 2026, up from $324.7m in 2025. The three areas that increased the most were impairment of assets, depreciation costs, and \"selling, general, and administrative\" costs.\n\nThe impairment of assets increased as part of the company's efforts to retrofit its air-cooled data centers in British Columbia and Childress, and develop direct-to-chip liquid cooling for the Childress data centers for its AI cloud services. Impairment alone increased $631.6 million YoY.\n\nDepreciation increased by approximately $236m, which was put down to the company's \"higher operating capacity\" at Childress, and the additional GPUs deployed.\n\nSelling, general, and administrative costs, meanwhile, increased by around $313 million, of which more than half went to the company's \"stock-based compensation expense.\"\n\n\"The increase in stock-based compensation expense was primarily related to the September 2025, October 2025 and May 2026 vesting of certain market-based RSUs and stock options and the resulting accelerated recognition of the remaining unrecognized compensation cost, the amortization of certain stock-based payment awards modified and awarded in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year 2025, and the amortization of RSUs issued to employees and directors during the year ended June 30, 2026.\"\n\nIn July 2026, both co-CEOs at Iren were further awarded each 9,099,328 units of restricted stock.\n\nAnother operating expense noted is the cost of power, which Iren said was approximately 27 percent of its total revenue.\n\nThe company held cash or cash equival","highlights":["The company held cash or cash equivalents of $5.89bn, and restricted cash of $1.7bn, most of which is for the Microsoft contract's capex related to GPUs.\n\nCFO Anthony Lewis noted that the company has this year secured circa $19 billion in funding, including prepayments, GPU funding, convertible notes, and equity.
